plan.notes: TRUE catalog program name: 'Computer Science, Professional Computer Science Concentration, B.S.' (Department of Computer Science). Transcribed verbatim from the official MTSU 2024-25 'Computer Science-Professional Computer Science Academic Map' (Suggested Fall/Spring Four-Year Schedule), source_url above. Transcription method: downloaded the official catalog PDF (pdftotext -layout) and transcribed course-by-course; subtotals cross-checked against the map's printed per-term subtotals. CATALOG-YEAR HONESTY: the live catalog on 2026-09-30 is the 2025-2026 Undergraduate Catalog (which still lists this concentration), but no 2025-26 term-by-term academic map for this concentration is published/indexed; the 2024-25 map is the latest official term-by-term sequence, so catalog_year is set to 2024-2025. No known curriculum changes vs. 2025-26: the 2025-26 catalog program page carries the same 41-hr True Blue Core / 44-hr major / 33-hr supporting structure; verify with an advisor before use. The PDF also carries a Fall/Spring/Summer variant (sophomore summer: elective + CSCI upper-division elective, etc.); this plan uses the primary 8-term Fall/Spring schedule. Caveats: (1) MATH placement/eligibility alternatives shown on the map (MATH 1730 with C or better, ACT Math subscore 26+, Math Dept. Calculus Placement Test, MATH 1710) are placement details, not course prereqs, and are recorded here, not in prereq lists; the plan records the in-plan math path (MATH 1910) where the map allows 'MATH 1730 or 1910' / 'MATH 1710 or 1910'. (2) 'CSCI 303_' is the map's placeholder for a high-level programming language course (student/dept choice) - recorded as choice slot CSCI 303X. (3) 'One must come from Discovery' markers on TBC choice slots are preserved in choice titles. (4) Science year-long sequence: any of BIOL 1110/1111+1120/1121, CHEM 1010/1011+1020/1021, CHEM 1110/1111+1120/1121, PHYS 2010/2011+2020/2021, PHYS 2110/2111+2120/2121; third science course must use a different prefix (BIOL 1110/1111, CHEM 1010/1011, CHEM 1110/1111, PHYS 2010/2011, or PHYS 2110/2111). (5) Map note: every course counted toward the 44 CS credit hours plus MATH 1910 and COMM 2200 requires a grade of C (2.00) or higher.
